ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
During the construction of the Sanmenxia Dam in the Yellow River flood control project, a soil-transporting truck was parked at the bottom of the concrete dam slope. The driver suddenly noticed a rock on the slope, 16 meters away from the base, which began to roll down from rest with a uniform acceleration of $2\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$ due to vibrations, as shown in the figure. Upon noticing the danger, the driver immediately started the truck to escape. Due to obstacles caused by soil and rocks, the truck's direction of motion was along the extension of the rock's rolling path. Assuming the driver's reaction time is 1 second, after starting, the truck accelerates uniformly at $1\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. Meanwhile, after reaching the base of the slope, the rock continues at a constant speed and then decelerates uniformly at $1.5\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. (Take $g = 10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.)

1. What is the velocity and time when the stone reaches the bottom of the slope?
2. Calculate whether the earth-moving vehicle can escape danger. If it can escape, calculate the closest distance between the rock and the vehicle before the rock stops moving; if it cannot escape, calculate how long after the vehicle starts moving the rock will collide with the vehicle. Do not add any other content.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the upper left of the figure there is a stone located on an inclined dam slope, and at the foot of the slope there is an earth-moving truck parked; to the right of the foot of the slope is horizontal ground, and the vehicle's direction of motion is to the right along the horizontal extension line of the path along which the stone rolls down. Then reason: take the time when the driver discovers the stone as the global time t=0. The stone starts from rest at a place 16 m from the foot of the slope and moves with uniform acceleration along the inclined slope, a=2 m/s^2, so 16=(1/2)·2·t^2, obtaining t=4 s; the speed at the foot of the slope is v=at=2·4=8 m/s. The vehicle has a 1 s reaction time, and after t=1 s it starts from the foot of the slope and moves with uniform acceleration, with position x_truck=(1/2)(t-1)^2. The stone reaches the foot of the slope at t=4 s, and afterward moves along the horizontal extension line and decelerates at 1.5 m/s^2, with position x_rock=8(t-4)-(1/2)·1.5·(t-4)^2. Let x_rock=x_truck: 8(t-4)-0.75(t-4)^2=0.5(t-1)^2. Let u=t-1 be the time after the vehicle starts, then t-4=u-3, and the equation becomes 5u^2-50u+123=0, obtaining u=5±sqrt(10)/5. For the first meeting take the smaller root u=5-sqrt(10)/5. The stone needs 8/1.5=16/3 s from the foot of the slope to stopping, and at the meeting the time elapsed after reaching the foot of the slope is u-3=2-sqrt(10)/5 s, which is less than 16/3 s, so the meeting is valid, and the vehicle cannot escape.
